newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn sets auction for 2-yr, 3.50 pct coupon notes.
newsitem.headline: Bonn sets auction for 2-yr, 3.50 pct coupon notes.

text.p: The German federal government set an auction for two-year 3.50 percent coupon Treasury notes, with bids due by 0900 GMT on Wednesday, the Bundesbank said on Tuesday.
The bond matures on Sept 18, 1998, the interest payment date is Sept 18 and the first interest payment will be made on Sept 18, 1997, said the Bundesbank, who is the issuing agent.
The settlement date is Friday Sept 20 and the notes will be bourse-listed on Monday, Sept 23, the Bundesbank said.

Germany has pledged to issue two-year Treasury notes at quarterly auctions as part of a package of measures to aid the development of the domestic bond market by selling more short-term government debt.
This week's issue is the first such issue of two-year debt.

The government in July, for the first time, sold six-month Treasury Bills, or Bubills, in what dealers said was a success sale. The Bubills, like the two-year Treasury notes, will be issued on a quarterly basis.
